description: PRD-128: Unified Notification System — Capture completion events from all sources (heartbeats, tasks, missions, playbooks, triggers, reports), route via per-workspace preferences (in-app, Telegram, Slack, webhook), and surface them in a real bell-icon notification center. Reuses notification_service.py and channel_connections.

userStories.title: Create notification_preferences and notifications tables
userStories.description: As a platform developer, I need the database schema to store notification routing preferences and in-app notifications so the dispatcher has somewhere to read/write.
acceptanceCriteria: New Alembic migration in orchestrator/alembic/versions/ with correct down_revision pointing at current head (not None)

Creates notification_preferences table: id (uuid pk), workspace_id (uuid fk->workspaces, cascade), user_id (int fk->users nullable cascade), event_type varchar(50), destination varchar(30) default 'in_app', channel_connection_id (uuid fk->channel_connections nullable set null), enabled bool default true, created_at/updated_at timestamptz
NO UNIQUE constraint on (workspace_id, user_id, event_type) — multiple rows per event allowed so a single event can fan out to in_app AND telegram

Creates notifications table: id, workspace_id, user_id (nullable), event_type, title varchar(255), message text, link_type varchar(30), link_id text (NOT varchar), agent_id (int fk->agents set null), agent_name varchar(100), status varchar(20) default 'ok', read_at, dismissed_at, created_at

Indexes: ix_notif_prefs_workspace, ix_notif_prefs_user (partial where user_id not null), ix_notifications_workspace, ix_notifications_user (partial), ix_notifications_unread_ws on (workspace_id, created_at DESC) where read_at IS NULL AND dismissed_at IS NULL
Migration runs cleanly up and down against a local postgres
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Implement NotificationDispatcher service
userStories.description: As a platform developer, I need a single dispatcher that reads preferences and fans out a single event to zero or more destinations so every caller has one entry point.
acceptanceCriteria: New file orchestrator/core/services/notification_dispatcher.py with class NotificationDispatcher(db, workspace_id)
async dispatch(event_type, title, message=None, link_type=None, link_id=None, agent_id=None, agent_name=None, status='ok', user_id=None) returns dict with dispatched_to list
_get_preferences returns a LIST of all matching preference rows (no LIMIT 1), prefers user-specific rows over workspace-default (user_id IS NULL) when both exist for the same destination

For each enabled pref: if destination=='silent' skip; if 'in_app' insert row into notifications table WITHOUT calling self.db.commit() — caller owns the transaction; if 'telegram'/'slack'/'webhook' call notification_service.send_workspace_notification(workspace_id, formatted_msg, channel=destination); if 'channel' look up channel_connection row and send to that specific connection (extend helper as needed)
_format_external_message returns a concise multi-line string with status icon, title, agent_name (if set), truncated message (200 chars), and (TODO placeholder) deep link
If NO preferences exist for an event_type, defaults to a single in_app dispatch
Unit tests cover: silent skip, in_app insert (no commit), multi-destination fanout (in_app + telegram from two rows), user-specific overrides workspace default, no-preferences default
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: NotificationDispatcher(db, workspace_id) in orchestrator/core/services/notification_dispatcher.py. _get_preferences returns full list with user-row override per destination; silent skipped, in_app inserts without commit, telegram/slack/webhook delegate to send_workspace_notification, channel resolves channel_connections.platform. No-prefs falls back to single in_app. 6 unit tests in tests/test_prd128_notification_dispatcher.py all passing.

userStories.title: Notifications API endpoints (list, unread-count, read, read-all, dismiss)
userStories.description: As a frontend developer, I need REST endpoints so the bell dropdown can fetch and mutate notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: New file orchestrator/api/notifications.py with APIRouter prefix='/api/notifications' tags=['notifications']

GET /api/notifications — paginated list (limit default 20 max 100, offset), optional unread_only=true filter, workspace-scoped via RequestContext, excludes dismissed rows, orders by created_at DESC, returns {success, notifications[], total, limit, offset}
GET /api/notifications/unread-count — returns {success, count}
POST /api/notifications/{id}/read — sets read_at=NOW() if unread, returns {success}
POST /api/notifications/read-all — marks all unread for user/workspace as read, returns {success, marked_count}
POST /api/notifications/{id}/dismiss — sets dismissed_at=NOW(), returns {success}
All queries enforce workspace_id = ctx.workspace_id AND (user_id = ctx.user_id OR user_id IS NULL)
Router included in orchestrator/main.py
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Notification preferences API endpoints (GET, PUT bulk)

acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/api/notifications.py (or new file) add router prefix='/api/notification-preferences'

Workspace-scoped — user cannot modify another workspace's prefs
